title: Bolt.new alternatives
summary: Bolt.new alternatives: candidate paths, switching costs and reasons to keep the original.

sections.heading: Match the reason to a candidate
paragraphs: Compare Lovable and Replit for a new guided prototype. Evaluate Cursor if you are willing to manage the code and infrastructure directly. Do not compare a code assistant subscription with a whole hosted application bill.

sections.heading: When to keep the original
paragraphs: Keep Bolt if its documented scope fits and you can independently build the exported project. Resolve usage limits before treating a different billing unit as cheaper.

sections.heading: Migration rehearsal
paragraphs: Create a copy of the project, remove production secrets, export data using a documented method and run the tests in the candidate workflow. Compare the work needed to restore service after a failed change. Keep the original until the rehearsal succeeds.

verdict: Change direction when the technology scope, handoff or iteration budget is the actual constraint.
bestFor: Existing Bolt.new users with a specific workflow, budget or ownership constraint
notFor: Readers expecting a replacement to move code, data and infrastructure automatically
migration: Trial the candidate on a branch; retain the original workflow until tests, export and billing checks pass.
gaps: Verify the account's Privacy Mode and team setting, use of personal API keys, enabled non-ZDR model approvals, Cloud Agent use and applicable agreement before drawing account-specific processing or retention conclusions; no account settings were inspected.

pros.text: Lovable documents code synchronization with GitHub, GitLab and Bitbucket for teams that want a repository handoff.
Replit describes Agent as a plain-language path that plans, creates, checks, fixes and deploys applications.

cons.text: Bolt documents JavaScript-based web application frameworks and a separate Expo path; confirm the project stack before treating it as a broad language-neutral builder.
The candidates document different starting workflows, so a comparable prototype and handoff test is needed before ranking their output.

faqs.question: Do these alternatives start from the same kind of workflow?
faqs.answer: No. The cited docs describe Bolt JavaScript app building, Lovable natural-language web app building, Replit Agent app creation, and Cursor as an editor and coding agent. Choose the workflow that matches the prototype you need to hand off.

faqs.question: Does changing builders automatically move a complete application?
faqs.answer: Do not assume that it does. Lovable documents code sync, while its ownership guidance calls for a separate plan for databases and services; rehearse the specific export and runtime migration.

faqs.question: What should I verify about Lovable model training before choosing a builder?
faqs.answer: Its 2026-09-15 Privacy Policy says Customer Content and Usage Data may be used for training, with a free settings opt-out that takes effect prospectively on any plan; it excludes Business/Enterprise content and usage data and app end-user data. The August 2026 Terms and November 2025 DPA distinguish data scopes differently, so verify the actual workspace agreement and setting.

faqs.question: Does choosing an EU Lovable Cloud region keep all project data in the EU?
faqs.answer: Lovable says Lovable Cloud offers EU, US and Asia Pacific regions and that selected-region Cloud data does not move across regions by default. Its Privacy Policy also says Lovable and service providers process Personal Data in multiple countries, including the US. This does not establish the actual workspace selection or locations for connected services and model providers.

faqs.question: What does Cursor Privacy Mode cover, and what should an account verify?
faqs.answer: Cursor says Privacy Mode prevents training on Customer Data and that most model requests use provider zero-data-retention agreements, subject to safety and abuse review and non-ZDR model exceptions. Requests made with personal API keys still pass through Cursor's backend and rely on the provider's terms for retention. Optional Cloud Agents store encrypted repository copies while a run is active, then delete them after completion. Teams and Enterprise can enforce Privacy Mode; Cursor says individual plans follow its Privacy Policy rather than the commercial DPA. Verify the account setting, organization policy, model approvals, API-key route, Cloud Agent use and applicable agreement; none was inspected here. Cursor also says Privacy Mode applies to Self-Hosted Machines and that code sent by the worker is not used for training when enabled, although run content still reaches Cursor and artifacts may upload to its storage; confirm whether this feature and setting apply to the account.
